behavioral_effects: GOV-CLOSE now names the three options governance change finish requires, so a close no longer costs a failed run and a --help round trip, and points at --help as the authority for the full list rather than carrying a copy. GOV-OPEN tells an agent resuming an interrupted session to compare branch and HEAD against the open session.
compatibility_impact: None. No contract, schema, route, event, validator ID, or generated artifact changes. governance-sync reported no bytes changed, so no manifest derives from this text.
follow_up: Consider recording the branch alongside start_commit in the change session state so the Stop hook or change finish can warn on a mismatch, retiring the manual check this change documents.
limitations: The shrink pass (two reviewers: duplication/drift and simplification/altitude) cut the first draft by about a third. It found the draft restated the CLI help text near-verbatim and listed five optional flags as though exhaustive while the CLI has seven, dropping --contract and --adr - an incomplete copy presented as complete. The shipped version defers to --help instead. The ARGS line in the code block was reduced to a placeholder because the 105-character original demonstrated the nested quoting the following paragraph tells the reader to avoid.

Net-positive diff of 22 lines. Nothing could be deleted or consolidated: no other skill documents these options, and ship and pick-workflow reference the target only for sequencing. The one line removed is the bare command the change replaces.

Block A documents a workaround, not a fix. The durable repair is for the CLI to record the branch in the session state and warn on mismatch; that lives in tools/repo_governance and is out of scope here.
reason: GOV-CLOSE shows a bare 'make governance-change-finish', but the CLI exits without writing unless --security-impact, --compatibility-impact and --rollback are supplied, so every close pays a failed run and a --help round trip before the real call; the optional flags that carry the Report's content are never named. Separately, an open session records start_commit but not its branch, so an interruption can leave the tree on another branch carrying the governed edit with nothing flagging it - which happened in this session
risks: The three required options are restated here and could drift if the CLI changes them. Mitigated by keeping the exhaustive list out: the text names only the three required flags plus the two tied to this skill own steps, and defers to ARGS=--help for the rest.
rollback: Revert the commit. Prose in one skill file with no generated output derived from it and no state to undo. The staged copy at ~/.claude/skill-updates/2026-08-22/gov-change/ is outside the repository and a revert does not touch it.
security_impact: None. Prose only, in one agent skill file. No code, configuration, dependency, hook, permission, or exposure surface changes. The text grants no capability; it documents options the CLI already requires and a check the agent performs by reading git state.
summary: Document the required change-finish options and the branch check when resuming a session in gov-change
